newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea business group sees dim outlook in June.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea business group sees dim outlook in June.

text.p: South Korean businesses expect the economy to remain in a slump in June compared to a year ago, but their outlook has improved from May, a corporate survey by the Federation of Korean Industries (FKI) said on Friday.

The Business Survey Index (BSI), provided by FKI, a powerful lobby group representing the nation's biggest conglomerates or chaebols, stood at 84 for June, against 86 for the same month a year earlier and 75 for May.
A BSI figure higher than 100 means businesses' outlook is bullish. Anything less than 100 means their outlook is bearish.

"Despite the easing of the yen's fall and a rise in exports on the back of recovery in international prices of major export items, the business outlook for June is expected to stay in a slump," a FKI statement said.

The federation blamed the downturn on a slowdown in domestic consumption and investment and an expected deterioration of financial conditions due to instability in financial markets and conservative fund management by financial institutions.

It said local consumption was likely to slow in all sectors except for construction and food and beverages, which would see a rise on seasonal factors. "Cheaper import products from Southeast Asia were forecast to depress light manufacturing industries, while an overall economic slowdown would dampen heavy manufacturing and chemical businesses," the federation said.
The group's export outlook was slightly more positive as the Japanese yen halted its fall against the dollar and companies were trying to boost their sales abroad.
Although international prices of South Korea's major export items were rising, it was still unclear whether the trend would continue, it said.
